I found one confirmed bug and one test-quality concern in the uncommitted changes. I only read the diff and didn't run the tests.

1. **`src/click/testing.py:119`, confirmed.** The new `__next__` override raises `EOFError` instead of `StopIteration`, and this stream is installed as `sys.stdin`. So a command under test that does `for line in sys.stdin:`, iterates `click.get_text_stream("stdin")`, or reads a `click.File("-")` argument will crash when the input runs out. It will not end the loop normally. The fix is to leave `__next__` alone. Raise `EOFError` only inside `visible_input` and `hidden_input`, for example when `readline()` returns an empty string.

2. **`tests/test_chain.py:166`, plausible.** The pipeline test no longer asserts `not result.exception`, and it slices off the last two output lines with `[:-2]`. It now accepts a run that ends in an abort, and any real failure that adds output lines would still pass. I'd assert the abort explicitly, or give the test enough input lines that it doesn't abort.

findings.summary: Overriding `__next__` on the stream installed as `sys.stdin` makes it raise EOFError instead of StopIteration, which breaks the iterator protocol.
findings.failure_scenario: A command under test does `for line in sys.stdin:` or iterates `click.get_text_stream('stdin')` or a `click.File('-')` argument. When the input runs out, `__next__` raises EOFError, so the loop crashes instead of ending. With `CliRunner.invoke(cmd, input='a\nb\n')` the command fails with an exception and exit code 1. Under a real terminal or pipe, the same command ends normally. The fix is to leave `__next__` alone and raise EOFError only in `visible_input` and `hidden_input`, for example when `readline()` returns ''.

findings.summary: The pipeline test now drops its `assert not result.exception` check and slices off the last two output lines.
findings.failure_scenario: The test now accepts a run that ends in an abort. It also hides any real failure that adds output lines, because `[:-2]` discards the last two lines whatever they say. A genuine regression would still pass. The test should assert the abort explicitly, or give the input enough lines to avoid it.
